'''Andrew Jonathan Nok'''{{Audio|LL-Q56475 (hau)-Eunice Ameh-Andrew Jonathan Nok.wav|Listen|help=no }} , [[Nigerian National Order of Merit Award|NNOM]] (11 February 1962 &ndash; 21 November 2017) was a [[Nigerian]] Professor of [[Biochemistry]] and the Public Affairs Secretary of the [[Nigerian Academy of Science]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nas.org.ng/fellowship/members-of-council/ |title=Members of Council |work=Nigerian Academy of Science |accessdate=6 June 2015 |url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150707061854/http://www.nas.org.ng/fellowship/members-of-council/ |archivedate=7 July 2015 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.vanguardngr.com/2011/12/five-professors-win-20102011-merit-award/|location=Lagos, Nigeria|title=Five professors win 2010/2011 Merit Award|author=Lawani Mikairu|date=1 December 2011|accessdate=6 June 2015|newspaper=[[Vanguard (Nigeria)|Vanguard]]}}</ref> In 2010 he was a recipient of the Nigerian National Order of Merit Award (NNOM), in the Science category<ref name=NNOM /> and in 2013 he won the Alexander [[Humboldt Prize]].<ref>[http://edugist.org/professor-andrew-nok-wins-alexander-humboldt-prize-for-2013/Professor Andrew Nok Wins Alexander Humboldt Prize For 2013]</ref> He died on 21 November 2017 after a brief illness.<ref>{{Cite news|date=2017-11-21|title=Breaking: Kaduna Commissioner for Education dies at 55|url=https://www.vanguardngr.com/2017/11/breaking-kaduna-commissioner-education-dies-55/|location=Lagos, Nigeria|access-date=2020-07-17|newspaper=[[Vanguard (Nigeria)|Vanguard]]|language=en-US}}</ref>

==Early life==
Nok was born on 11 February 1962 in [[Kaduna State]], Northern [[Nigeria]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.thisdaylive.com/articles/5-win-national-merit-award/103462/ |title=5 Win National Merit Award |date=23 November 2011|accessdate=6 June 2015 |url-status=dead|author=Patrick Ugeh|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150713232106/http://www.thisdaylive.com/articles/5-win-national-merit-award/103462/ |archivedate=13 July 2015 |newspaper=[[This Day]]}}</ref>
His parents were from Nok village in the [[Jaba, Nigeria|Jaba]] [[Local Government Area]] of [[Kaduna State]]. He attended the LEA Primary School in [[Kaduna (city)|Kaduna]] before he proceeded to  Government Secondary School, [[Kafanchan]] where he obtained the [[West African School Certificate]] in 1979, the same year he was admitted into [[Ahmadu Bello University]] where he received a [[bachelor's degree]] in [[biochemistry]] in 1983, [[master's degree]] in 1988 and [[doctorate degree]] in 1993.<ref name=NNOM>{{cite web|url=http://nnma.gov.ng/users/andrew-jonathan-nok-(nnom)/722495703|title=Prof. Andrew Jonathan Nok (NNOM)|work=Nigerian National Order of Merit|accessdate=6 June 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://m.thenigerianvoice.com/news/76623/1/president-jonathan-plans-to-immortalize-deserving-.html|title=President Jonathan Plans To Immortalize Deserving Nigerians|work=The Nigerian Voice|date=1 December 2011|accessdate=6 June 2015}}</ref> He was married to Amina Nok and is a father of three children: Anita, Amanda and Nathan Nok.

==Political career==
Nok was nominated as Commissioner of Health and Human services by the Executive Governor of [[Kaduna state]], Mallam [[Nasir Ahmad el-Rufai]] on 29 July 2015, along with other 12 nominees.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/more-news/187457/ |title=el-rufai-nominates-13-commissioners.html |accessdate=29 July 2015 |newspaper=[[Premium Times]]}}{{dead link|date=July 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>
